title: National Register of Historic Places Registration Form: National Historic Landmark Nomination, Fountain Lake Farm
notes: NPS National Historic Landmark nomination (NRHP reference 90000471) for Fountain Lake Farm, Marquette County, Wisconsin; a scanned typescript PDF. Found with WebSearch 'John Muir Fountain Lake Farm National Historic Landmark nomination'. The fetch tool does not read PDFs, so the text layer was extracted with pdftotext (poppler) from the PDF downloaded from this url on 2026-10-15 and saved as a manual snapshot; OCR noise is kept as is and quotes use only clean passages.

title: Lorne Hotel, formerly a residence where John Muir was born in Dunbar, Scotland
notes: NPGallery asset record, Yosemite Historic Photo Collection (negative RL_13024, create date April 1, 1905); found in the same related-assets list.

title: June-September 1879 [Journal 28]: Expedition to Alaska
notes: University of the Pacific Scholarly Commons record for Muir's 1879 Alaska journal (John Muir Papers, MSS 048, Holt-Atherton Special Collections); found with WebSearch 'scholarlycommons.pacific.edu John Muir journal 1879 Alaska'.

claim: In 1838, on April 21, John Muir was born in Dunbar, Scotland.

evidence.quote: 1838: April 21, John Muir born in Dunbar, Scotland.
1838 April 21 Born in Dunbar, Scotland to Daniel Muir & Ann Gilrye Muir.

notes: Tour stop 1 (Dunbar). Combines the date and place that MUI-F-0001 and MUI-F-0074 state separately, from two holders fetched by http.

claim: The Lorne Hotel in Dunbar, Scotland, was formerly a residence where John Muir was born.

evidence.quote: Lorne Hotel, formerly a residence where John Muir was born in Dunbar, Scotland on April 21, 1838.

notes: Tour stop 1 (Dunbar): the building. Same record says the boyhood home and the birth building were adjacent ('actually born in the building to the left').

claim: The residence in Dunbar where John Muir was born remained the Muir family home until 1849.

evidence.quote: Lorne Hotel, formerly a residence where John Muir was born in Dunbar, Scotland on April 21, 1838. This remained the Muir family home until 1849.

notes: Tour stop 1 (Dunbar): date range 1838-1849 for the stop.

claim: In 1839 John Muir and his family move from Muir's birthplace at 126/128 High St., Dunbar, next door to 130 High St.

evidence.quote:
1839
April 21 : John Muir turns 1 year old
John and his family move from Muir's birthplace at 126/128 High St., Dunbar, next door to 130 High St., where the family remained until Muir was 11 years old.

notes: Tour stop 1 (Dunbar): street addresses. Only the Sierra Club chronology gives the street numbers.

claim: In 1841 John Muir begins school in Dunbar.

evidence.quote: 1841 Begins school in Dunbar.

notes: Tour stop 1 (Dunbar).

claim: In 1849, in the company of his father, sister, and brother, ten-year-old John Muir left Scotland for the United States.

evidence.quote:
In 1849, in the company of his father, sister, and
brother, ten-year-old John Muir left Scotland for the United
States.

notes: Tour travel leg 1 to 2. NHL nomination (primary). The same page's footnote says John turned eleven during the trip; sources differ on his age (see MUI-F-0024 notes).

claim: In 1849 the Muirs landed in New York City and went by boat to Albany and then across the Erie Canal to Buffalo.

evidence.quote:
In 1849, in the company of his father, sister, and
brother, ten-year-old John Muir left Scotland for the United
States.

The Muirs landed in New York City and went by boat
to Albany and then across the Erie Canal to Buffalo.

notes: Tour travel leg 1 to 2 (arrival and inland route). The year comes from the same narrative's opening sentence on the preceding page.

claim: From Buffalo, Daniel Muir and his three children traveled across the Great Lakes to Milwaukee and then overland to Kingston.

evidence.quote:
In Buffalo,
conversations with a Scotsman and a local grain dealer convinced
Daniel Muir to look for a site in the Marquette County region of
Wisconsin. With his three children he traveled across the Great
Lakes to Milwaukee and then overland to Kingston.

notes: Tour travel leg 1 to 2 (last part). John Muir was one of the three children (same source: Sarah and David were with John and their father).

claim: John Muir lived continually at the Fountain Lake farm from 1849-1856.

evidence.quote:
John Muir (1838-1914), a leading figure in the origin of an
environmental ethic in the United States, traced the development
of his own interest in wilderness preservation to the Fountain Lake
farm where he lived continually from 1849-1856

notes: Tour stop 2 (Fountain Lake farm): date range.

claim: John Muir lived periodically at the Fountain Lake farm from 1862-1864.

evidence.quote:
John Muir (1838-1914), a leading figure in the origin of an
environmental ethic in the United States, traced the development
of his own interest in wilderness preservation to the Fountain Lake
farm where he lived continually from 1849-1856 and periodically
from 1862-1864.

notes: Tour stop 2 (Fountain Lake farm): later stays.

claim: Daniel Muir, John Muir's father, named the farm Fountain Lake.

evidence.quote:
Daniel Muir, John's father, named the
farm Fountain Lake.

notes: Tour stop 2.

claim: The farmhouse on the Muir farm, made of white pine, was completed in October 1849.

evidence.quote: Muir farm buildings. These included a log shanty, farmhouse, barn,

A more substantial farmhouse,
made of white pine from the northern forest, was completed in
October 1849

notes: Tour stop 2: the building. Basis for any reconstruction: log shanty of bur oak and white oak, white pine farmhouse on high ground, hand-hewn log barn with piled-straw roof (same page).

claim: In early November 1849 the rest of John Muir's family arrived from Scotland.

evidence.quote:
In
early November 1849, after the planting and the construction of the
principal farmhouse, the rest of the family arrived from Scotland.

notes: Tour stop 2.

claim: At the Fountain Lake farm, Muir tried, for the first time, to preserve from human development a piece of land in its wild state.

evidence.quote:
In Wisconsin, Muir demonstrated his
preservation ethos at the Fountain Lake farm where he tried, for
the first time, to preserve from human development a piece of land
in its wild state.

notes: Tour stop 2.

claim: John Muir identified the Fountain Lake farm as the birthplace of his interest in preserving wilderness for its own sake.

evidence.quote:
John Muir, however,
identified the Fountain Lake farm as the birthplace of his interest
in preserving wilderness for its own sake.

notes: Tour stop 2.

claim: John Muir and his family moved to their second Wisconsin farm, Hickory Hill.

evidence.quote:
John Muir's significant association with Fountain Lake
continued after he and his family moved to their second Wisconsin
farm, Hickory Hill

notes: Tour stop 2 (Hickory Hill). The NHL excludes Hickory Hill from the landmark for the compromised integrity of its historic structures.

claim: John Muir assumed more and more of the work at the new farm, Hickory Hill.

evidence.quote:
Responsible for much of the clearing, John Muir assumed more and
more of the work at the new farm, Hickory Hill

notes: Tour stop 2 (Hickory Hill).

claim: In 1857 John Muir helps his family construct a house, barn and well at Hickory Hill.

evidence.quote: 1857 Helps family construct house, barn & well at Hickory Hill.

notes: Tour stop 2 (Hickory Hill).

claim: In 1849, in February, the Muir family emigrates from Glasgow to New York, the trip taking six weeks by sailing ship.

evidence.quote:
1849
April 21 : John Muir turns 11 years old
February : The Muir family emigrates from Glasgow to New York, the trip taking six weeks by sailing ship

notes: Tour travel leg 1 to 2 (the crossing). The ship's name is not given by any source found. Month conflicts with University of the Pacific chronology ('1849 Spring Leaves Scotland'); kept as each source's own version.

claim: In 1860 Muir exhibited inventions at the State Fair in Madison.

evidence.quote: 1860: Left home to exhibit his inventions at the State Agriculture Fair in Madison, Wisconsin
1860 September Leaves home; exhibits inventions at State Agr. Fair, Madison, Wise.

notes: Tour stop 3 (Madison). Narrower than MUI-F-0026 so that both holders cover the whole claim.

claim: In 1861 Muir enrolls at the University of Wisconsin.

evidence.quote: 1861 January Enrolls at University of Wisconsin, Madison.

1861
April 21 : John Muir turns 23 years old
February : Enrolls at the University of Wisconsin

notes: Tour stop 3. Conflict: the NPS timeline (MUI-S-0017) puts enrolment under 1860; Pacific says January 1861, Sierra Club February 1861.

claim: Muir lived in North Hall, the student residence hall, at the University of Wisconsin.

evidence.quote:
February : Enrolls at the University of Wisconsin and attends for almost 2 1/2 years (5 trimesters); teaches school in winter
Learns about geology from Dr. Ezra S. Carr . Carr's wife, Jeanne, becomes his mentor
Invents a study desk that retrieves a book, holds it in place for the prescribed period of time, and then automatically replaces it with another book
Muir has his first informal lesson in botany from from Milton S. Griswold, a classmate, beneath a black locust near North Hall, the student residence hall where he was then living.

notes: Tour stop 3: the building. Room within North Hall not stated by a registered source (gap). The NHL nomination dates the Griswold botany lesson to June 1862, not 1861, so no year is claimed.

claim: In 1863 Muir leaves the University.

evidence.quote: 1863 June Leaves University, intending to enter medical school

1863
April 21 : John Muir turns 25 years old
Leaves the university

notes: Tour stop 3: end date. The NPS timeline says '1863: Left the University'.

claim: In 1868, in March, Muir arrives in San Francisco via the Isthmus of Panama.

evidence.quote: 1868 late March Arrives in San Francisco via Isthmus of Panama.

1868
April 21 : John Muir turns 30 years old
Sails to California via Cuba, New York, and the Isthmus of Panama
March 28 : Arrives in San Francisco, California.

notes: Tour travel leg to stop 4 (Yosemite). No ship name found in a registered source.

claim: In 1868 Muir first visited Yosemite.

evidence.quote: 1868 Apr-Jun First visit to Yosemite via Pacheco Pass, Snelling and Crane Flat.
Muir first visited Yosemite in 1868.

1868
April 21 : John Muir turns 30 years old
Sails to California via Cuba, New York, and the Isthmus of Panama
March 28 : Arrives in San Francisco, California.
Walks to Yosemite from San Francisco.
April - June : First visit to Yosemite

notes: Tour stop 4 (Yosemite). Same statement as MUI-F-0032 with the Pacific and NPS quotes that each cover it.

claim: In the fall of 1869 John Muir began his fulltime life in Yosemite Valley, where he ran a sawmill for James Hutchings.

evidence.quote: In the fall of 1869 John Muir began his fulltime life in Yosemite Valley where he rebuilt and ran a sawmill for James Hutchings.

notes: Tour stop 4.

claim: James Hutchings hired John Muir to build and operate his sawmill.

evidence.quote: James Hutchings hired the 31-year-old Scotsman named John Muir to build and operate his sawmill.

notes: Tour stop 4.

claim: John Muir's cabin was by Yosemite Creek.

evidence.quote: He made his own cabin by Yosemite Creek and guided hotel guests on hikes.
During his time there, he built a cabin by Yosemite Creek to fall asleep to the sound of rushing water.

notes: Tour stop 4: the building. NPS records a plaque only at the 'supposed site' of the cabin (NPGallery RL_01365), so no exact location is claimed.

claim: In 1880, on April 14, John Muir married Louie Wanda Strentzel.

evidence.quote: 1880: April 14, married Louie Wanda Strentzel
1880 April Marries Louie Wanda Strentzel, April 14.

notes: Tour stop 6 (Martinez): start of the Martinez years.

claim: In 1880 Muir rents part of the Strentzel ranch and lives in the Coleman house on the ranch.

evidence.quote: 1880 Apr-Ju1 Rents part of Strentzel ranch; lives in Coleman house on ranch; works in orchards and vineyards to learn fruit business.

notes: Tour stop 6: residence before 1890.

claim: The John Muir House was built in 1882 by Dr. John Strentzel.

evidence.quote: Significance: The house was built in 1882 by Dr. John Theophile Strentzel, outstanding early horticulturist and physician.
John Muir House, Alhambra Boulevard, Martinez, Contra Costa County, CA
Dr. John Strentzel, John Muir’s father-in-law, built the John Muir House in 1882.
evidence.locator: The Strentzel and Muir Home paragraph

notes: Tour stop 6: the building.

claim: In 1890 the Muir family moves into the big house.

evidence.quote: 1890 October Dr. John Strentzel dies; Muir family moves in to "Big House."
When Dr. Strentzel passed away in 1890, Mrs. Strentzel invited the Muir family to move into the "big house" with her.

notes: Tour stop 6: start date for the house.

claim: John Muir made the John Muir House in Martinez his home from 1890 until his death in 1914.

evidence.quote: John Muir House, Alhambra Boulevard, Martinez, Contra Costa County, CA
John Muir, who married Strentzel's daughter, made this his home from 1890 until his death in 1914.

notes: Tour stop 6: date range.

claim: In the John Muir House, Muir produced most of his significant published works on the flora and fauna of the west.

evidence.quote: John Muir House, Alhambra Boulevard, Martinez, Contra Costa County, CA
Here Muir, naturalist, conservationist and rancher, produced most of his significant published works on the flora and fauna of the west.

notes: Tour stop 6: what he did there.

claim: John Muir converted one large bedroom on the second floor into a study.

evidence.quote: The second floor has six bedrooms, one water closet and one bathroom. Three bedrooms have been restored: Muir's, the children's and the guestroom'. One large bedroom was converted to a study by John Muir and has been restored as such.

notes: Tour stop 6: the room. The NPS page captions Muir's desk in the 'Scribble Den' (MUI tmp-tour-S-2); HABS photo 13 (1960) is titled 'John Muir bedroom & study'.

claim: Muir had the large family parlor fireplace built in the mission style after the original fireplace was destroyed in the 1906 earthquake.

evidence.quote: The large family parlor fireplace is in the mission style that Muir had built after the original fireplace was destroyed in the 1906 earthquake.

notes: Tour stop 6: room detail for reconstruction.

claim: In 1899 John Muir was aboard the steamship George W. Elder with the Harriman Alaska Expedition.

evidence.quote: Muir's seventh trip to Alaska, with the Harriman Alaska Expedition to Wrangell, Glacier Bay, Sitka, Prince William Sound, and the Aleutian Islands and beyond. In 1899, railroad magnate Edward H. Harriman organized a summer voyage to the wilds of Alaska: He converted a steamship, the George W. Elder, into a luxury "floating university," populated by some of America's best and brightest scientists and writers, including John Muir. Those aboard encountered

notes: Tour stop 5 (Alaska) travel leg. Smithsonian Institution Archives (MUI-S-0080) also says the expedition 'traveled to Alaska aboard the S.S. George W. Elder' but does not name Muir in that passage.

claim: In 1890 Muir traveled to Muir Glacier in Alaska.

evidence.quote: 1890: Traveled to Muir Glacier in Alaska

notes: Tour stop 5 (Alaska).

claim: In 1879 Muir and S. Hall Young travel together to Sitka, Stickeen River, Fairweather Mountains and Glacier Bay.

evidence.quote: 1879 Jun-Jan 1880 First Alaska trip; Bulletin correspondent; itinerary includes Portland, Seattle, Victoria. Meets S. Hall Young at Ft. Wrangel; travel together to Sitka, Stickeen River, Fairweather Mountains, Glacier Bay.

notes: Tour stop 5 (Alaska).
